{"self_assessment": "Impact
I carried the top line of the fish from the middle of the body out toward the nose. That was about 22 dominoes laid in four batches while the table was running low on supply. I also stood a couple of dominoes back up near the nose and closed a small gap where the bottom line meets the tip. Those pieces were part of what made the outline read as a continuous fish body.

Execution
Before building I inspected the belly and the middle of the body and confirmed the doubled section was fully connected and would fall with the start. I then built in short batches so I could check each one as it landed. After the top line reached the nose, I inspected the join several times and made only light fixes, taking nothing down, so I didn't disturb the rest of the structure. I went hands-off before the push, as agreed.

Collaboration
I stayed off the tail and the bottom line when asked, so I didn't double up with anyone else's work. I told the table what I was doing before each action, including when I offered to run the top line to the nose, when I was fixing the gap, and when I was done. That let the others plan around me. I also reported what I found in the body inspection so the others could rely on it.

Leadership
I kept the mood light and the energy up through the closing minutes, with clear and frequent updates. I volunteered to take the unclaimed top-line stretch when it was the table's bottleneck, and I kept the table focused on hands-off discipline before the push. I believe I contributed about a fifth of the table's result.", "my_share_percent": 20}
